obligations.text: IPM is installed by a %ALL user with a one-line installer downloaded from the registry, or offline from a zpm.xml file.
obligations.gap: No model of the installer channels (README one-liner, offline zpm.xml through preload/cls/IPM/Installer.cls::setup). ns_mapping.rs::installer models only the mapping/record effect of setup, not how it is obtained. Contrast: the offline zpm.xml and registry one-liner yield the same installed IPM version and record.

parent.entailment: The lead adds the install channels and the %ALL premise; graded directly (absent). No composition credited.

units.P1: excluded: list heading for the installer steps

obligations.text: The installer installs only when its version is newer than the IPM already present.
obligations.cases: installer version newer vs equal/older than the installed IPM
obligations.gap: No model of the version gate in preload/cls/IPM/Installer.cls (setup/ZPMLoad). Contrast: running the 0.10.x installer over the same installed version leaves the zpm record and code untouched, vs a newer installer replacing them.

obligations.text: The installer maps the %IPM package into the current namespace.
obligations.cases: namespace with no %IPM mapping vs one with an existing mapping
obligations.observation: package and routine mappings after setup
obligations.gap: ns_mapping.rs::installer transcribes the ClassMapping/RoutineMapping only-when-absent rule and proves l1_install under premise INST; the existing-mapping case is the F-NSP-5 witness (mapping left pointing at the source). The rule is proved, but the premise INST excludes exactly the mapped case, so the intended "maps %IPM into the current namespace" for a previously mapped namespace is not established. Contrast: setup in a namespace mapped from USER leaves %IPM pointing at USER (witness) vs a fresh namespace getting its own mapping.

obligations.text: The installer sets default settings without overwriting existing ones (so upgrading IPM keeps existing values).
obligations.cases: setting already set vs unset at install time
obligations.gap: The writer rule (overwrite disabled keeps a nonempty value) is proved in public_repairs.rs, but the installer call (preload/cls/IPM/Installer.cls::ZPMInit, L110-124, seeding each key with overwrite off) is not modeled; playbook settings.rs takes the seed map as static input. Contrast: config set analytics 0, then re-run the installer: analytics stays 0, vs a fresh namespace getting 1.

obligations.text: The installer loads IPM in normal mode without automatic mappings.
obligations.cases: installer load vs default load arguments
obligations.observation: IPM module developer mode and automatic mappings after setup
obligations.gap: The installer's `load <dir> -DDeveloperMode=0 -DNoMapping=1` call (Installer.cls ZPMLoad) is not modeled; NoMapping itself is modeled for load in iter59 mappings.rs (module.placement#2) but nothing ties the installer to it. Contrast: after setup, zpm's record has DeveloperMode=0 and no %IPM package mapping was added by its resources.

obligations.text: Upgrading from legacy IPM 0.7 moves its data into the new storage.
obligations.cases: upgrade from 0.7 storage vs fresh install
obligations.gap: No model of the 0.7 migration (Installer.cls MapIfLegacy and data moves; tests/migration/v0.7-to-v0.9 ModuleStorage is a test). Contrast: a namespace with 0.7 ^ZPM data ends with the same modules listed by `list` after upgrade.

obligations.text: Upgrading from IPM 0.7 maps IPM to all namespaces.
The installer installs the Python packages ORAS needs and the ipm and iriscli helper scripts.
obligations.cases: default vs custom ModuleRoot; Python available vs not
obligations.observation: pip packages and helper scripts present
obligations.gap: No model of the wheel and helper-script install (root module.xml L23-59, Installer.cls:564). Contrast: a custom ModuleRoot breaks the helper-script install (metadata observation) vs the default root succeeding.

obligations.text: IPM adds the zpm command to the instance's language-extension routines (%ZLANGC00 and %ZLANGF00).
obligations.cases: routine without the generated block vs with it; both routines
obligations.gap: rewrite_from appends the generated block when no Start tag is found, but no assertion exercises that branch (the witness already has a block) and the two-routine transaction (Main.cls:3464-3502) is not modeled. Contrast: a routine with only user lines gains exactly one generated block after them.

obligations.text: It rewrites only the block it generated and keeps every other line, so a user's own extensions survive repeated installs.
obligations.cases: user lines before/after the block vs generated lines; first vs second run
obligations.observation: lines outside the generated tags; number of blocks
